svg.text: S4 AISLE SHUTTLE — boxes hang by their rims, a hook pulls them out
Two rack faces, 3 lanes × 16 levels each, across a 188 mm aisle. A carriage in the aisle reaches every box in one move.
worst case 6.1 s · mean ≈ 4 s · machine ≈ €1,450
TOP VIEW of level 9 (wall at the top, door at the bottom)
lanes A B C, 179 mm each · box 176 × 162 hangs on 2 runners
Boxes hang by their side rims on stainless runners, like pans in a GN trolley.
The carriage carries a short piece of the same runners. It lifts 5 mm, its
passive J-hook catches the box rim, and it pulls the box onto itself.
Then it rises to the top: the carriage itself is the exit.

g.text: 1/7 The carriage waits empty at the top. Wanted: a box in the front face, lane C, level 9
2/7 Z down and X across at the same time: the carriage stops 5 mm below the box’s runners
3/7 Carriage up 5 mm: the hook tip rises behind the box rim
4/7 The hook pulls the box straight out onto the carriage runners
5/7 Up to the top under the roof hatch; the box is ready
6/7 The transport reaches through the hatch and lifts the box out
7/7 Put-away is the same in reverse: down, push the box in, drop 5 mm to release, back up
